eli: Trying to onboard openchat-lite-6b via hf2redwood v0.6.2 — conversion fails mid-way.
eli: Error snippet: 
```
RuntimeError: shard mapping mismatch: expected 8 shards, found 8 files but keys don't line up (first key assigned to shard_4)
During remap: Missing token: <eos> in tokenizer.special_tokens_map
```
eli: Also the repo's chat formatting file is absent (no chat_prompt.json), so the converter generates an empty prompt template.
priya: can you paste the repo layout + config.json + tokenizer.json? also which hub revision did you pin?
eli: repo ls:
```
model/
  weights-00001-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00002-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00003-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00004-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00005-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00006-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00007-of-00008.safetensors
  weights-00008-of-00008.safetensors
  index.json
  tokenizer.json
  config.json
```
eli: config.json excerpt: `{"vocab_size":50257,"eos_token":null,"tie_word_embeddings":true}`
eli: tokenizer.json specials: `{"special_tokens": []}` — no eos / sep tokens.
priya: ok that explains the missing token error. converter expects `eos_token` present or a chat template to define it. two things to try: add `--force-eos ""` (temporary) or update tokenizer with `{"eos_token":"<|end|>"}`.
tony: fwiw I traced the shard-index mismatch to HF's `index.json` ordering when downloads race under our parallel fetcher. index.json lists shard metadata but the converter was using filesystem glob order to map names -> shards. if hub returns items in a different order the mapping shifts.
tony: quick check: `python -c "import json,sys;print([s['file'] for s in json.load(open('index.json'))['safetensors']])"` — compare to `ls weights-*.safetensors`.
eli: interesting — in my case index.json lists weights in a different sequence than filenames. that would cause key ranges to be assigned to wrong shard.
priya: then pinning to a revision makes it worse if the index was updated asynchronously. which revision did you pin?
eli: I pinned to `v1.0` (the tag on repo) using `--pin-revision v1.0` when running convert. converter then failed with 404 for one shard when trying to fetch by id, even though the web UI shows all files.
priya: that sounds like a hub indexing lag: tag points to a tree but LFS objects may still be resolving. workaround: `--download-index-first --verify-checksums` or avoid pinning until repo index stabilizes. also try `hf_hub_download(..., allow_patterns=["*.safetensors"])` to force full list.
eli: i tried `--no-rename-weight-keys` which bypasses weight-key rewrite errors but later quantization step fails because runtime expects canonical key names: `KeyError: 'model.embed_positions.weight' not found in state_dict`
tony: we should add an index-order validator to the converter: ensure mapping from index entries to actual files is deterministic and based on filename matching, not iteration order. also validate checksums up-front and fail early with a clear message.
priya: i'll open a GH issue with minimal repro: attach the repo index.json, tokenizer.json, config.json + a small script that reproduces the converter run. label: `hf-convert: shard-index-ordering + missing-eos`.
priya: temporary fixes: 1) add eos to tokenizer.json and re-upload 2) run `hf2redwood --download-index-first --verify-checksums` 3) if you must pin, pin to the exact commit sha for the tree, not just tag.
eli: confirmed `--force-eos "<|end|>"` lets conversion finish past the tokenizer stage. will try quantize after fixing keymap.
tony: i'll add the index checker patch to my PR queue, should be a small change (compare list lengths, checksums, and canonical sort by filename).
devops-bot: CI failed: `hf2redwood-convert` job #342 on openchat-lite-6b — failing with shard->key mismatch. linked pipeline: https://ci.internal/342
eli: thanks — opening issue now and attaching logs. appreciate the quick triage :pray:
priya: thanks, eli. keeping this thread for updates, will follow-up when PR lands.
